Case built for teaching: the underlying CT is real (public archive) and has no lesions; the lesions were added by computer with the noise of the original image. The realism is good but simplified: no histology, the outcome is the one set in the simulation.
Hemangioma is the most common benign solid liver lesion. The key sign is that in all phases it follows the density of blood (blood pool): in the arterial phase, discontinuous peripheral nodules with the same density as the aorta, then progressive centripetal filling, until it becomes isodense to the vessels in the delayed phase. Large lesions may have a center that does not fill in (fibrosis or thrombosis).
Differential diagnosis: metastasis (continuous ring, hypodense center, no complete filling), hepatocellular carcinoma (homogeneous arterial hyperenhancement and washout), "flash-filling" hemangioma (small, fills in completely in the arterial phase). The simple cyst has water density and does not enhance.
